**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve small components in the effective mixture**

At runtime this replacement inherits the base config's `mixture_block_size=49_152`, while `MixtureDataset._compute_expected_counts_per_block` truncates every `weight * block_size` and assigns the entire remainder to the largest component. For this new 391-component split, 79 positive-weight components therefore receive zero samples, the requested 22.5856% long-document share becomes 22.4365%, and the 159-sample remainder inflates the largest short component. Thus the launched treatment neither samples every populated cell nor preserves the advertised per-bucket mass; use a block size or mixture representation that retains these small cells.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make the skew parameter explicit**

The long-context multiplier defines the experiment's treatment, but this signature silently defaults it and the treatment config consequently calls `long_context_phase_weights()` without specifying the intended `2x` value. Make `skew` required and pass `LONG_CONTEXT_SKEW` at the experiment boundary so this critical parameter cannot be inherited implicitly.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L90-L93](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/54d3106d44432a725673f5682d14858d4574ec98/AGENTS.md#L90-L93)

comments.body: 🤖 Fixed in 7ac0ef3a9d. The treatment now keeps the baseline's 168 top-level component names and phase-1 weights, so its 49,152-sample block allocation is identical to the control. Each top-level component is a concatenation of one short-store child and two long-store children; the 2× skew is applied inside the component without introducing separately rounded mixture weights.
